name: Ptolemaeus
bio: Ptolemaeus is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors gives no date for the poet. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of Meleager's Wreath, the Garland compiled about 100 BC.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the second volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book VII: 314).

poems.title: Book VII, 314
poems.author: Ptolemaeus
poems.text: Learn not whence I am nor my name; know only that I wish those who pass my monument to die.

poems.title: Book IX, 577
poems.author: Ptolemaeus
poems.text: I Know that I am mortal, a creature of a day; but when I search into the multitudinous revolving spirals of the stars my feet no longer rest on the earth, but, standing by Zeus himself, I take my fill of ambrosia, the food of the gods.

poems.title: Species Aeternitatis (Mackail)
poems.author: Ptolemaeus
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: I know that I am mortal, and ephemeral; but when I scan the multitudinous circling spirals of the stars, no longer do I touch earth with my feet, but sit with Zeus himself, and take my fill of the ambrosial food of gods.
